notes: CBP-24 is Pliant Technologies' CrewCom Flex four-channel wired intercom beltpack (part of the CrewCom Flex frameless IP intercom platform, launched at InfoComm 2026). Physical I/O was read directly off manufacturer product photography on the official product page (bottom panel labeled "Headset", "PGM Vol", "Primary (PoE) 100BT", "Secondary 100BT"). "PGM Vol" is a rotary volume knob (control), not a connector, so it is not listed as a port. The device has built-in mic/speaker for hands-free use and a network-delivered "auxiliary program" audio feed — there is no physical aux audio jack. Power is PoE/PoE+ delivered over the Primary Ethernet port; the device has no separate power connector, so no standalone power port is listed. Connector-id caveats: the schema has no generic 4-pin-XLR audio id, so xlr4-dc was used as the nearest physical match for the XLR-4M headset jack (not an actual DC power use); the two Ethernet ports show a locking-collar/latch typical of etherCon, so "ethercon" was chosen over plain "rj45" — treat this specific choice as a visual inference. Grade "eth-100m" is directly confirmed by the "100BT" (100Base-T) panel labeling. No dimensions, weight, or rack info are published on the manufacturer page (this is a desktop/wearable beltpack, not rack-mountable). A companion 2-channel model, CBP-22, also exists in the same family.

ports.name: Headset
ports.note: Industry-standard XLR-4M headset jack (mic in + speaker out combined on one 4-pin XLR male).

ports.name: Primary (PoE) 100BT
ports.note: Ethernet port with visible metal locking collar/latch consistent with a ruggedized etherCon-style RJ45 (standard RJ45 cables also mate). This port also supplies PoE/PoE+ power to the beltpack — there is no separate power inlet on the unit.

ports.name: Secondary 100BT
ports.note: Second Ethernet port, same ruggedized-RJ45 style, used for daisy-chaining beltpacks (up to 3 units) or downstream devices.
